knowledge_graph.title: Prosthetic joint infection
knowledge_graph.description: Prosthetic joint infection, also known as peri-prosthetic joint infection, is an acute, sub-acute or chronic infection of a prosthetic joint. It may occur in the period after the joint replacement or many years later. It usually presents as joint pain, erythema, joint swelling and sometimes formation of a sinus tract.
knowledge_graph.causes: microorganisms (usually bacteria, but also fungi) causing infection of a prosthetic joint
knowledge_graph.other_names: artificial joint infection, Infected joint prosthesis, joint replacement infection
knowledge_graph.symptoms: joint pain, joint swelling, erythema, sinus tract formation, prosthetic loosening, warmth of the joint, fever

text_blocks.snippet: A prosthetic knee infection, also known as periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), is a serious complication that can occur after knee replacement surgery. It involves the growth of microorganisms, typically bacteria, on the artificial joint, leading to inflammation and potential damage. Infections can occur at any time after surgery, but early infections (within a few weeks) and late infections (months or years later) have different causes and characteristics.
snippet_highlighted_words: a serious complication that can occur after knee replacement surgery
